summary: Master financial statement analysis with our advanced training course. Enhance your skills and make informed decisions for your business success.
lede: Reading company accounts means connecting balance sheets, income statements, cash flows and disclosures to assess performance, earnings quality, liquidity and risk. This course is for financial, credit, investment and accounting professionals who need to compare results and support valuation or credit decisions. Participants practise ratio and common-size analysis, DuPont breakdowns, cash-flow diagnostics, earnings-quality review and statement-based forecasting to turn reports and footnotes into concise recommendations.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to interpret financial statements, test earnings quality, and support valuation or credit decisions with defensible analysis.
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic working knowledge of accounting terminology, the structure of financial statements, and spreadsheet use in Excel. Prior exposure to ratio analysis, annual reports, or corporate finance will help, but no programming is required. The course assumes you can read an income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement, and that you are ready to work with calculations, disclosure notes, and company comparison exercises.
